summary: Ornella Bahidika and Joel Allou discuss the design of Ace, a production AI voice tutor that runs complete lessons reliably. The core thesis is that reliability in multi-step agents is a control problem, not a prompting problem. Engineers who try to ship flow agents encounter recurring failures: the model declares the lesson done prematurely, skips a step, or loops. The first instinct—prompt harder—does not address the root cause. Ornella introduces the metaphor that the model is the talent, brilliant at delivering a line but terrible at tracking its position in a multi-step procedure, while the harness is the director. A lesson in Ace is a small state machine with six nodes: intro, teach, check, grade, advance, and wrap. Each node sends the model a narrow contract specifying one action and the expected return. The harness validates the output, advances state, and decides what comes next. The model never determines where it is in the flow. Joel demonstrates harness engineering in practice. Instead of using a large reasoning model like Opus 4.7 for everything, they constrain each step to a specific action with carefully scoped input. This enabled them to use Haiku 4.5, a smaller model with less reasoning capability, while maintaining expected performance—saving money, time, and latency. Joel identifies three categories of decisions the LLM should never own: when the lesson is done, whether the student actually learned correctly, and what comes next. These are engineered outside the model. The approach generalizes beyond voice tutors to coding agents, ops runbooks, and onboarding flows. The heuristic: if your agent's reliability feels like a coin flip, remove decision-making from the model and build those decisions as external abstractions. Let the model talk, but don't let it drive.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & Problem with Multi-Step Agents
sections.summary: Ornella introduces Ace, a live AI voice tutor, and describes common failure modes of multi-step agents: declaring done early, skipping steps, and looping.

sections.title: Control Problem, Not Prompting Problem
sections.summary: Ornella argues reliability is a control problem, not a prompting problem, and introduces the talent/director metaphor for the model and harness.

sections.title: Lesson as State Machine with Narrow Contracts
sections.summary: Ornella describes the lesson state machine (intro, teach, check, grade, advance, wrap) and how each step gives the model a narrow contract validated by the harness.

sections.title: Harness Engineering & Model Selection
sections.summary: Joel explains harness engineering: building steps externally, providing only scoped input per step, enabling use of Haiku 4.5 instead of Opus 4.7 to save cost and latency.

sections.title: Demo Logs & Three Decisions the LLM Shouldn't Own
sections.summary: Joel shows logs of harnessing for sections, whiteboard, queue clearing, and endings. Identifies three decisions engineered outside the model: lesson completion, student correctness, and next step.

sections.title: General Applicability & Conclusion
sections.summary: Joel explains the approach applies to coding agents, ops runbooks, and onboarding flows. Heuristic: if reliability is a coin flip, take control flow out of the model.

demonstrations: Recording showing harness logs for a live lesson, including section input, whiteboard drawing, queue clearing, and lesson-ending steps
